trickyParts: Sub-architect exemption in resumeWorker: `role === "architect"` bypasses the not-active-phase skip (mirrors retireIdleWorker). A child issue's architect is never phases[child].phase once it has spawned a planner and resumeWorker is its ONLY recovery path (handleException sends only the root architect to resurrect); without the exemption every dead sub-architect would be stranded. Lock: processes.test.ts 'resumes a sub-architect ...' now seeds phases[child]=planner and asserts the catch-up is still prompted and the phase untouched.

Race guard placement: resumeWorker's pre-check (assignment pending -> drop; bystander -> skip) runs BEFORE workerCatchup's GitHub fetch, outside the role lock. The invariant lives inside deliverToWorker's mutateClaim callback: `if (pending.kind === "catchup" && claim?.pendingAssignment?.kind === "assignment")` drop -- covering all three pendingAssignment write sites (booting branch, enqueueIdleWorker, enqueueClaimForLaunch/launchWorker) when an architect spawn_worker lands during the fetch. Tested deterministically by mutating the claim from the test's workerCatchup.tokenManager.getToken hook (processes.test.ts 'drops a catch-up inside the role lock ...').

Live evidence for Acceptance 8: this very issue's implementer claim (LEGION-37) had its queued architect task overwritten by {"type":"catchup-worker","unhandled":[]} at 2026-09-13 01:00 UTC after a role-lane delivery exception, so the resumed worker received a bare catch-up instead of its assignment -- exactly the overwrite the lock-side guard now refuses.

PendingAssignment is a discriminated object, not a sibling kind field or a second slot: every reader is forced by the type to say which kind it handles, and the spec's 'a catch-up is DROPPED when an assignment is pending' has no precedence rule to encode. v25->v26 migration (migrateV25State) classifies each persisted string by payload (JSON.parse in try/catch; only a record with type === "catchup-worker" is a catchup). Proven on the rig (pre-rebase, when the step was v24->v25) against a state.json the main checkout wrote: the .bak held the bare string, the migrated file the {kind:"assignment", task} object. After the rebase the same proof must be re-taken by the tester against a main-written v25 file: expect state.json.v25.bak with the bare string and state.json at version 26 with the object.

/state does NOT expose phases (api/state.ts redacts to the documented keys), so the plan's tester lever 'observe via legion state that phases[issue] is unchanged' has to read the daemon's own state.json on disk (the rig did) -- worth knowing before the tester plans E2E.

Rig observation, not changed here: a `--resume` relaunch of a killed worker did not answer negotiate_protocol within worker_rpc_timeout_seconds (5 s) at /worker/ready, so the catch-up stayed queued until the boot watchdog's 3x120 s retire-and-retry relaunched it (then delivered). Pre-existing behaviour on the untouched ready path; the tester may hit it on resumed sessions.
Boot-time reconnect TypeError seen on the rig is LEGION-11 / pull request #955's fix; not changed here.

Delivery-time bystander predicate (review scope extension, spec v6): `isBystanderCatchup(state, issue, role, pending)` in legion-state.ts = `pending.kind === "catchup" && role !== "architect" && !isActivePhase(...)` -- the same predicate resumeWorker's pre-check uses, applied again where a queued catch-up would actually be delivered: `promoteQueuedWorker` (inside the admission lock, before either branch, so a bystander catch-up neither prompts a live idle pane nor relaunches a retired claim; the entry is consumed like a stale one and the pending cleared) and `workerReady` (ready confirmed as connect-only, pending cleared and persisted, nothing prompted). An `assignment` in the same position is delivered unchanged; an architect's catch-up is always delivered (sub-architect ready test). Rationale: the phase can move on while a catch-up waits behind the cap or a boot, so the enqueue-time check alone still relaunched finished workers.

Why the ready-time bystander drop must RETIRE the pane, not just clear the pending prompt (review round 2, blocking): a relaunched `omp --mode rpc` that is never prompted emits no `agent_start`/`agent_end`, and `workerReady`'s `clientFor` only connects + negotiates (never `get_state`), so its cached client stays at `runState: "unknown"` -- `runningWorkerCount` counts every locator-bearing claim whose client is not idle, and `armIdleRetire` fires only from an idle transition. Dropping the prompt alone therefore left a do-nothing pane holding a `workerCap` slot indefinitely (reviewer reproduced: `spawnWorker` for another role at cap 1 -> `queued`). The drop branch now performs exactly `retireIdleWorker`'s retirement inside the same `mutateClaim` critical section: `retireWorkerLocator` (graceful shutdown, kill-pane fallback), locator cleared, `ompSessionFile` -> `resumeSessionFile`, `readyConfirmedAt` set and `launchFailures` reset (the boot did succeed), persisted, watchdog cancelled -- so the slot frees the moment it persists and the role's next `spawn_worker` `--resume`s the same agent. Regression lock: the ready test now asserts one shutdown frame, locator cleared, `resumeSessionFile` kept, and that a following `spawnWorker` for another role at cap 1 is `spawned`, not `queued`; it fails with the retire replaced by a bare drop. The bystander predicate itself is defined once as `isBystanderRole` (legion-state.ts) and shared by `resumeWorker`, `isBystanderCatchup`, and `/worker/started`'s log.

Why the ready-time bystander retire must DRAIN the worker queue explicitly (tester round 3): retiring the pane frees its workerCap slot in state, but every other retirement path gets its drain for free -- retireIdleWorker/markWorkerDead retire a pane whose cached client's socket close reaches onWorkerClientClosed -> markWorkerDead -> promoteWorkerQueue(). The ready-time retire never called clientFor, so no cached client exists to close and nothing triggers a drain; a spawn already queued behind the cap was promoted only by the next 60 s linger sweep (reconcileWorkerAdmission; the rig measured 5.3 s and 33.3 s). workerReady now calls this.workerAdmission.promoteWorkerQueue() after the mutateClaim critical section returns (a `retiredBystander` flag set inside it), exactly the shape markWorkerDead uses. Regression lock: the round-3 ready test now queues the planner at cap 1 BEFORE ready arrives and awaits the promotion's own worker-started publish with no sweep call; with the drain line removed it times out, with the retire replaced by a bare clear it fails at the shutdown/locator assertions.

Confirm-before-retire ordering in the ready-time bystander branch (review round 3, blocking): `retireWorkerLocator` cancels the boot watchdog for every generation of the token, then revokes the capability, then stops the pane -- and the stop can throw StopFailed (a real kill-pane failure; the pane may still be alive, so the locator is never cleared). With the in-memory confirmation written AFTER the stop, a StopFailed left the claim locator-intact but `readyConfirmedAt` undefined, `pendingAssignment` still the catch-up, no watchdog armed and no cached client -- nothing revisits that shape, and every later spawn_worker for the role took the booting branch and queued its task forever for a /worker/ready that already came. Fix: `delete pendingAssignment; readyConfirmedAt = now; delete launchFailures` BEFORE `retireWorkerLocator`, keeping the locator clear/carry and the single persist after the await. On StopFailed the claim is then exactly retireIdleWorker's own StopFailed shape (locator intact, confirmed, catch-up gone) and the next spawn_worker recovers through the live-claim probe path; a daemon restart re-derives 'unconfirmed' from disk (nothing was persisted) and reconnectWorkers re-arms the watchdog. Regression lock: a test injects StopFailed at the ready-time retire (shim unreachable at stop, kill-pane exit 1 with a non-'gone' stderr) and asserts locator intact + readyConfirmedAt set + launchFailures cleared + catch-up cleared, then a spawn_worker for the role answers `resumed` by prompting the live pane (not the booting branch's queued-pending `resumed`); fails with the round-3 stop-then-confirm ordering. The now-redundant `cancelBootWatchdog(token, generation)` after the retire is dropped (retireWorkerLocator already cancels all generations).

Composing with main's LEGION-33 bump (PR #1001): main took state version 25 as a pure bump (migrateV24State adds no fields; every v24 record validates as v25), and production state.json is already version 25 under that meaning. So the classifying step could not stay at v24->v25 -- a deployed daemon would have skipped it (state.version !== 24) and then rejected its own bare-string pendingAssignments under the strict v26 schema. It is renumbered to migrateV25State (v25->v26), appended after migrateV24State in the migrations array, with LegionState.version/z.literal/newLegionState/loadState all at 26 and the backup named .v25.bak. One test proves the composition: a v24 file with bare-string pendingAssignments migrates through both steps to v26 objects with a .v24.bak; the classification tests write version-25 input files (main's v25 shape with bare strings).
deviations: Smoke rig ran in SMOKE_WEBHOOK_MODE=none as requested, with root/child issues and a queued tree seeded into state.json (none mode has no Dispatch ingress, and resync heals only issues already in state.issues). The root-architect and controller panes were inert (sleep) and their HTTP calls driven by hand, per docs/solutions/testing/scratch-daemon-rig-proves-what-unit-tests-cannot.md; every phase worker was a real omp --mode rpc process on production's 18.1.18-sami.20260912-203541 invocation.

The rig daemon listened on up.sh's default 19370/19371 (rig-env.sh scrubbed its own LEGION_DAEMON_PORT export) instead of the intended 19437; production is 13370/13371 and no other rig was running, so isolation held.
